Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ideal noun

a standard of perfection

also ideals, an ideal, the ideal

classical

Cic. Or. 18: īnsidēbat in ejus mente speciēs ēloquentiae (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 3.81: speciēs, fōrma et nōtiō virī bonī (Lewis & Short)

speciēs, speciēī f.

noun, fifth declension

an ideal: the pattern of a thing seen by the mind

Cicero’s word for Plato’s ἰδέα (Ac. 1.30). The noun “ideal” is a modern sense; Latin names what the ideal is of: speciēs virī bonī, the ideal of a good man. The everyday senses of speciēs are sight, appearance, outward show and beauty, and in logic a kind (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • fōrma, fōrmae f. — the ideal form of a thing

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 43: excellentis ēloquentiae speciem et fōrmam adumbrābimus (Lewis & Short)

    Beside speciēs, the perfect shape of a thing; ordinarily shape, figure, appearance and beauty.

  • exemplar, exemplāris n. — a model, a pattern to copy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 331, 154

    Traupman’s word for an ideal: the model one copies (see model).

Examples

  • hanc illī ἰδέαν appellābant, nōs rēctē speciem possumus dīcere

    they called it idea; we can rightly call it speciesCic. Ac. 1.30 (Lewis & Short)

  • īnsidēbat in ejus mente speciēs ēloquentiae

    an ideal of eloquence was fixed in his mindCic. Or. 18 (Lewis & Short)

See also model, example.

SourcesLewis & Short: species · Lewis & Short: forma · Lewis & Short: exemplar · Lewis & Short: idea
